transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Yeah, um… I guess what brings me in is this thing that keeps happening at work. I’m in retail, and if I even think there might be a bat in the stockroom—or something flapping around back there—my heart just jumps, I start sweating, and I feel like I have to get out right then. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I know stockrooms always have random noises, boxes settling and all that… and one time a coworker joked about “something with wings” and I couldn’t stop thinking about it.
Do you experience these kinds of reactions in other situations, or does it seem to happen mostly in the stockroom when you're worried about something like a bat?

Mostly it’s when I think it could be a bat, yeah—like in the stockroom or that back hallway. I mean, I know realistically a bat in the store probably isn’t going to hurt me. I’m not, like, living in a cave or something… though we did have an old garage growing up where birds got in once, and that kind of stuck with me, I guess.

But if I see anything that even looks like one, or just a quick flutter out of the corner of my eye back there, my brain reacts like I’m in actual danger. It’s like my mind skips over the “it’s probably nothing” part.
Do you find yourself avoiding any other places or situations because you're worried about encountering a bat or something similar?

Yeah… I mean, not like I avoid everywhere, but I do change stuff around. I’ve been swapping out of closing shifts when I can, because that’s when the back area feels worse to me. And there’s this loading area—I’ll take the longer way around instead of walking past it, even though it’s kind of ridiculous and adds time.

If I have to check the stairwell, I’ll still do it, but I rush it. I’ll have my phone in my hand like that’s going to do anything, and I’m just scared the whole time. It reminds me of when my uncle used to keep all this junk in his shed and you’d hear little noises—sorry, that’s probably not the point. But yeah, I do avoid some of those spots or get through them as fast as I can.
Do you ever feel this kind of intense fear or panic in situations that aren't related to bats or things flapping around?

Not really… I mean, not that same kind of jolt. It’s mostly tied to that bat thing, or something that looks like it’s flapping around. Like, I can tell myself a bat in the store probably isn’t going to hurt me, but if I see something move fast in the back hallway—like a shadow or a quick flutter—my brain just treats it like I’m in real danger.

It’s funny, because other stressful stuff at work, like angry customers or the register messing up, I can handle that better. Well, I complain about it, everybody does… but it’s not the same. This is more like my body reacts before I’ve even figured out what I saw.
